method_card.title: Weighted Mean and Geometric Mean
method_card.content:
Sometimes a simple arithmetic mean is not appropriate because not all values contribute equally. In these cases you need a more specialised average.

The weighted mean assigns a weight to each value: \(\bar{x}_w = \frac{\sum (w \cdot x)}{\sum w}\) where \(w\) is the weight for value \(x\). This is similar to a frequency table mean — frequencies are a type of weight. Weighted means are used in grade calculations, index numbers and price indices.

The geometric mean is used when values represent multiplicative change, such as growth rates or ratios: \(G = \sqrt[n]{x_1 \cdot x_2 \cdot \ldots \cdot x_n}\). On your calculator, raise the product to the power \(\frac{1}{n}\).

The geometric mean is more appropriate than the arithmetic mean whenever data represent ratios or rates of change. If growth factors are 1.2 and 1.8, the arithmetic mean (1.5) overestimates; the geometric mean \(\sqrt{1.2 \times 1.8} \approx 1.47\) is correct.
steps: For a weighted mean: identify each value \(x\) and its weight \(w\)
Multiply each value by its weight to get \(wx\)
For the geometric mean: multiply all \(n\) values together, then take the \(n\)th root using your calculator
State whether arithmetic or geometric mean is more appropriate and explain why in context

exam_context.marks: 2–4 marks for weighted mean; 2–3 marks for geometric mean; up to 2 marks for justifying choice of mean
exam_context.frequency: Higher-tier topic; appears on approximately half of Higher papers, usually with index numbers or growth rates

worked_examples.question: A student scores 70% on coursework (weight 3) and 50% on an exam (weight 2). Calculate the weighted mean score.
A company's profit grew by factors of 1.4 (Year 1) and 2.1 (Year 2). Calculate the geometric mean growth factor to 3 s.f.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Geometric mean \(\approx 1.72\) (3 s.f.). The company grew on average by a factor of 1.72 per year.

worked_examples.question: Items: A at £20 (weight 5), B at £35 (weight 2), C at £10 (weight 8). Calculate weighted mean price. Why is it better than the arithmetic mean (£21.67)?

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Weighted mean ≈ £16.67. It is more appropriate because Item C (cheapest) is purchased 8 times while Item B (most expensive) is purchased only twice. The arithmetic mean treats all items equally, giving a misleading higher average.

bronze.display: Calculate the weighted mean of value 6 (weight 4) and value 10 (weight 6).
A student scores 80 on a test (weight 1) and 60 on an exam (weight 3). What is the weighted mean?
Calculate the geometric mean of 4 and 9.

misconceptions.message: \(G = \sqrt{4\times9} = \sqrt{36} = 6\). The arithmetic mean gives 6.5 — not the same.

bronze.display: A price index grows by factor 1.1 in Year 1 and 1.1 in Year 2. What is the geometric mean growth factor?

misconceptions.message: \(G = \sqrt{1.1 \times 1.1} = 1.1\). Equal values give same geometric and arithmetic mean.

bronze.display: Three component weights are 2, 3 and 5. What is \(\sum w\)?
When is the geometric mean more appropriate than the arithmetic mean?
options: When data represent multiplicative growth rates or ratios
When the dataset contains an outlier
When the data are negatively skewed

misconceptions.message: The geometric mean is designed for multiplicative data (growth factors, ratios).

bronze.display: Calculate the geometric mean of 2, 8 and 8 to 1 d.p.

misconceptions.message: \(G = \sqrt[3]{128} \approx 5.04\). Use cube root on your calculator.

bronze.display: A weighted mean gives \(\sum(wx) = 240\) and \(\sum w = 12\). What is the weighted mean?

silver.display: Marks: Maths 72 (weight 4), English 65 (weight 3), Science 80 (weight 3). Weighted mean mark?
Revenue growth factors over 3 years: 1.5, 1.2, 1.8. Geometric mean to 3 s.f.?
Weekly spending: Group A (40 people) £30, Group B (30 people) £50, Group C (30 people) £20. Weighted mean?
Investment grows by factor 3 in Year 1 and shrinks by 0.75 in Year 2. Geometric mean to 3 s.f.?

misconceptions.message: \(G = \sqrt{3\times0.75} = \sqrt{2.25} = 1.5\). Include the shrinkage factor (0.75) as the multiplicative value.

silver.display: Arithmetic mean of growth factors 1.0 and 4.0 is 2.5; geometric mean is 2.0. Which represents average growth?
options: Arithmetic mean (2.5), because it averages directly
Geometric mean (2.0), because growth is multiplicative

misconceptions.message: \(G=2.0\): applying factor 2.0 twice gives 4.0 — correct. Applying 2.5 twice gives 6.25 — wrong.

Grade components P (weight 5) score 74, Q (weight 3) score 62, R (weight 2) score 88. Weighted mean or simple mean (74.67)?
options: Simple mean; treats all components equally
Weighted mean (73.2); reflects each component's relative importance
Weighted mean only appropriate when weights are equal

misconceptions.message: Weighted mean = (370+186+176)/10 = 73.2. Component P carries most weight by design.
